policy: Only explicit reading is credited. Missing components remain pending; manuscript completeness does not establish scientific correctness or novelty.

records.source_notes: Read full main text and references, all main figures, all extracted supplement text, and all 34 unique images accounting for 55 embedded image members by hash. Original Word page layout not rendered; overlay/row alignment remains a limit for quantitative reuse. FOLR1 outlier measurements are not reproduced here. Source treatment-duration discrepancies retained. See davis-figure-receipts.json and davis-supplement-image-receipts.json.

All 20 patient rows and nine primer pairs inspected in the original one-page supplement. One KIT p.D579del; no additional KIT/PDGFRA hotspot mutations. Index patient never received imatinib. Assets have SHA-256 receipts in asset-retrieval-ledger.json. The index EWSR1 junction is upstream of the NR4A3 start codon, unlike the four other transcriptomes. RNA junctions do not establish protein products or drug dependence.

Single NR4A3-rearranged case with somatic KIT c.1669T>G (absent from blood). Three years stable disease on imatinib is reported; no serial response curve or functional assay of this variant in EMC is supplied. Do not generalize to every KIT variant or KIT-positive stain.

Two EWSR1-NR4A3 cases; one shows reported response, interruption-associated progression and response after restart. Figure 4 distinguishes infection from progression. Age, interruption duration and one dosing-unit entry differ across abstract/body/captions; precise exposure reconstruction needs reconciliation. Possible overlap with the 2014 sunitinib series remains unresolved.

Single PGR-NR4A3 case with reported benefit on tamoxifen. Figure 1A additionally lists pelvic radiation at tamoxifen initiation and lung-nodule resection two months later; narrative does not fully describe these interventions. Their contribution needs reconciliation before attributing the prolonged outcome to tamoxifen alone. This is not evidence for unselected EMC.
NCC-EMC1-C1 is distinct from USZ20-EMC1 and USZ22-EMC2. Public supplementary Tables 3 and 4 contain 221 screen rows and 24 IC50 rows; main text access remains unresolved.
Mixed-sarcoma screen includes HEMCSS/CVCL_1238. Model has an EWSR1-translocation caution; not counted as confirmed NR4A3-fusion evidence. Dataset is the same study, not an independent replication.

Subanalysis of JapicCTI-121850: two EMC patients, both stable disease (PFS 13.0 and 7.4 months). The partial response and all three supportive-care controls were mesenchymal chondrosarcoma. Overlaps the 2015 parent trial and 2017/2020 pooled analyses.

Pooled JapicCTI-121850/121853 analysis. Table 1 contains two EMC patients, both from the original trabectedin arm; zero EMC patients in supportive care or crossover. These are not two additional EMC patients beyond the Morioka subanalysis.

Reanalysis of the same Japanese trials: Table 1 again contains two EMC patients in the comparative trial and none in crossover. Figure 2 lists nine partial responders, all other histologies; its response-count difference from the 2017 report needs endpoint reconciliation.

records.source_notes: Eleven participants, zero WHO complete/partial responses. Read all EMC outcome values, flow and nonzero adverse-event rows. PFS 18-week rate 62.34% is not an integer fraction of 11 and conflicts with a simply interpreted median of 18 weeks; no correction inferred. Registry says nonrandomized while outcome population text says randomized. OS population description conflicts with denominator/censoring comments. Full related article remains pending.

NCBI BioC main text recovered after Europe PMC XML was unavailable. All four confirmed responses were other histologies; EMC outcomes are pooled in the main response table. The 32% stable-disease phrase has an ambiguous denominator and is not accepted as an EMC disease-control rate. Table text formatting needs visual verification. Discussion resistance hypotheses derive from other sarcoma models, not validated EMC mechanisms.
Original images, references and supplements pending. SGK1 RNA/protein discordance and isoform explanation; PPARG reporter work is in rat transfectants, not a demonstrated patient-cell dependency.

RETRACTED on 2026-05-04; identified by live publication-status check 2026-09-12 after cached-body reading missed the notice. Excluded from supporting the SGK1/proteasome mechanism or treatment lead. Original body-reading extent retained; completing figure review cannot rehabilitate retracted evidence.
Repository relocation to PRJNA692081. Raw sequence files not downloaded. No new efficacy result.

Figure images and original table layout pending. 32 evaluable courses in 21 patients; source sometimes calls courses patients. Abstract 87 versus body 86 patients. Imatinib SD >=6 months, interferon PD, sorafenib PD in Table 4; variant status not given.

All indexed figure assets inspected; no supplementary-material element in article XML. Molecularly confirmed cohort has four PR among ten evaluable. Table/caption discrepancies preserved in anthracycline-2013-tables.json. Cohort overlap with later Italian reports pending.

Reports three EMC patients (two stable disease, one progression) from TrObs. Parent supplement labels only one EMC, with myxoid and extraskeletal mesenchymal chondrosarcoma as separate rows. The matching total does not prove which patients were reclassified. Resolve classification before pooling; this is not an independent cohort. All text, three tables and figure read.

Patient 7 is EMC: pazopanib alone, stable disease, time to progression eight months. Pazopanib/sirolimus patient 10 and both ramucirumab patients are conventional chondrosarcoma. Pooled survival is not an EMC estimate; molecular confirmation not reported. No supplementary-material element found in the article XML.

59-patient retrospective cohort, only 23 molecularly tested, all EWSR1-NR4A3. First-line anthracycline one PR among ten evaluable; all three second-line anthracycline recipients had PD. Treatment selection may confound the adverse chemotherapy/survival association. Eight selected drug holidays do not establish general safety. Three trabectedin cases may overlap other Italian reports; unresolved. No supplementary-material element found in the article XML.

Parent TrObs study. Supplement Table S1 explicitly labels one EMC case with stable disease; later post-hoc paper reports three EMC. The parent also lists myxoid chondrosarcoma and extraskeletal mesenchymal chondrosarcoma separately. Reclassification or discrepancy remains unresolved; do not count the reports as independent cohorts.

Japanese registry: 171 included after excluding missing size/grade or <6 months follow-up. Six perioperative chemotherapy patients; indication bias, sparse events and wide intervals limit causal claims. Individual drug response and molecular confirmation are not supplied. Raw patient data are not public. Supplement Table S1 text and XML cells read; no embedded images. Original Word page layout not rendered. Figure 2 p=0.356 differs from table/body p=0.365. Discussion calls cited phase-II trabectedin trial phase III; do not propagate.

Single case with repeated local responses after surgery/SABR. The patient previously received six cycles of epirubicin/ifosfamide with reported partial response; the title does not mean no prior systemic treatment. Initial diagnosis was revised; molecular confirmation is not reported. Local control is not whole-body disease control or comparative survival evidence. CARE checklist is an image-only PDF; its embedded page image was inspected. No additional experimental supplement supplied.

Publisher notice identifies reused experimental images. Corresponding 2016 myeloma article excluded from evidence-supported SGK1/proteasome treatment lead. Context-only notice, not an EMC research output.

All body, abstract, references, three tables and eight figures inspected; appendix text/cells all read. Original Word layout not rendered. Patient identity overlap with earlier2018series pending. Three cases described as EMC. Main text/waterfall report one PR and two SD, but appendix codes two PR (patients 6, 14) and one SD (33). Molecular confirmation is not supplied. Response result unresolved; do not silently select a rate. Subtype HR 0.31 (95% CI 0.07–1.44), p=0.14, does not establish superior benefit. Substantial pooled toxicity is not an EMC-specific rate.

Earlier Peking University mixed-sarcoma apatinib series reports three unspecified chondrosarcomas, all PR. No EMC subtype or patient crosswalk supplied; cannot add three EMC responders or establish overlap with2020EMCcases. All three2020EMCappendixrows have no prior systemic therapy, whereas2018text says untreated five were ASPS/epithelioid, which also prevents simple assumed matching. Three figures depict osteosarcoma, Ewing and soft-tissue groups, not individually identified EMC. No supplementary-material element; rawdata restricted.

The sole EMC patient (52-year-old woman, Table2 patient10) received nanosomal docetaxel plus cyclophosphamide and had progressive disease. The pooled50% response rate and15.8-month survival are not EMC results. This is not an EMC gemcitabine/docetaxel response. Molecular confirmation, individual treatment line and response duration are not supplied. Retrospective manufacturer-funded study; no comparative evidence for formulation superiority or safety. No supplementary-material element in XML; raw data by author request only.

Single localized shoulder recurrence after unplanned R1 excision: preoperative radiotherapy was followed by a specimen without viable tumor and wide re-excision; no relapse at24months. This is a reported pathological complete response, not proof that surgery can be omitted or survival improves. Molecular confirmation is not reported. The authors already propose testing vascular histology as a radiosensitivity correlate. No tables or supplementary-material elements in indexed XML. Histology response is described in text, not shown in a pathology figure.

Single unresectable neck case: concurrent low-dose doxorubicin and radiotherapy produced a marked early response; follow-up was only one month after completion. Grade3 mucositis and dermatitis occurred. Carboplatin/paclitaxel was planned from TLE3/PGP/TUBB3/ERCC1 IHC, not reported as administered or effective. No NR4A3 confirmation reported. Cannot separate chemotherapy from radiation benefit or establish durable control. No tables or supplements in indexed XML; all five figures including pathology inspected. Vascular-response hypothesis already proposed by authors.

Single metastatic case with repeated local radiation responses during third-line trabectedin, after pazopanib and doxorubicin progression. New lesions and mediastinal progression occurred between radiation courses. No comparator separates radiation-alone effects from synergy; the authors proposed the combination before this review. Molecular confirmation and the pazopanib trial identifier are not supplied. Do not count this as an independent pazopanib cohort or continuous whole-body progression-free survival. Figure images are low resolution; tiny treatment-plan annotations are not reliably legible. No supplement link found on publisher page.

Context trial being screened for buried EMC data. No EMC subgroup established. Main table other-subtype footnote, original figures, later references and remaining supplements pending. Pooled sarcoma response is not EMC evidence. Publisher reports affiliation correction August2020.

One NR4A3-rearranged case treated at three metastatic sites with brachytherapy. Reported local control was 41 months for inguinal disease and 36 months for breast/popliteal lesions; lung metastases were not treated or quantified as a response endpoint. One grade 2 dermatitis event and no reported late toxicity do not establish comparative safety or superiority over external radiation. The narrative incorrectly gives D90 as a percentage; Table 1 gives Gy. Supplement two-page PDF text and all five embedded images accounting for four figures read.

Three selected patients without systemic treatment followed for 50, 70 and 126 months. Case 3 underwent palliative amputation, later had breathlessness and an EMC-positive pathological hip fracture, and died from colon cancer complications. Thus not all follow-up was event-free or asymptomatic despite abstract/discussion wording. EWSR1 rearrangement is reported; NR4A3-specific testing and lung biopsy are not. Patient-perspective immune-control statement has no accompanying immune assay. This is natural-history context, not evidence that observation is generally safe or equivalent to treatment. No tables or supplements in indexed XML.

Single pelvic/gluteal case treated by resection, argon-laser electrofulguration and peritoneal lavage. Uneventful postoperative course reported, but no long-term recurrence or survival outcome or NR4A3 confirmation. Does not establish benefit from the adjuncts. A phase-II study is proposed without a reported trial identifier or results. Intraoperative treatment here is not intraoperative radiotherapy. No tables or supplements in indexed XML.

Thirteen-patient retrospective surgical series; all five chemotherapy recipients had metastatic disease. Worse survival in that group does not establish chemotherapy harm or ineffectiveness. Drug names and response endpoints are not supplied. Tumor-size cut-off was selected in the same small dataset, without external validation. Table1 follow-up range14–86 months differs from24–96 in body/Table2; age maximum75 differs from73 in abstract/body. Figure1 caption describes hyaline cartilage with small undifferentiated cells; NR4A3 confirmation is absent. Diagnostic classification requires expert reconciliation, not an automated re-diagnosis. All body, abstract, references, three tables and four figures read; no supplement element.

Narrative review, not a new treatment cohort. Complete body, references, four table texts, four main figures and graphical abstract read; no supplement element. Radiation section duplicates the same long external-radiation narrative under Qiu2014 and Takagawa2022; the primary Takagawa report is instead the87-year-old ankle/three-site brachytherapy case. Do not count the repeated narrative as another patient. Prognosis section and Table1 give different post-metastasis survival figures, and the conclusion alternates pazopanib as initial versus post-anthracycline therapy. These statements require primary-source reconciliation. Some anatomical examples cite mesenchymal chondrosarcoma rather than myxoid; inclusion cannot rely on this review alone. Its references are discovery pointers, not completed primary reading or validated treatment recommendations.

Table1 identifies three EMC cases among39 lower-extremity sarcomas in a74-patient cohort, using spelling Extrasceletal. All patients received surgery and radiation. Individual EMC chemotherapy/hyperthermia exposures and outcomes are not reported; pooled survival and complication rates are not EMC estimates. Probable earlier preprint10.21203/rs.3.rs-1898999/v1, not independent patients. Table2/body report21/74 as24.3% while site counts sum18. No NR4A3 confirmation or supplementary material supplied. Raw data available by author request only.

Abstract distinguishes one extraskeletal case from two skeletal cases. Linked DOI10.1054/modi00100099 and printed alternate10.1016/s1084-8592(96)70025-5 belong to the same cited report; do not count separately. Full text unresolved.
